items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo leaves behind two nearly unbreakable records after retiring from Portugal
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s farewell from Portugal leaves behind two numbers that no active player is close to challenging. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has closed a 23-year international career that took him from a teenager replacing Luis Figo in a friendly to the greatest figure in Portugal’s history. His retirement, announced on Thursday, leaves behind a legacy of titles and unforgettable moments, but also two records that look more out of reach than ever, in men’s international soccer worldwide. The question now is whether anyone can ever get close.



The first is the goals record, in which the striker is the all-time top scorer for a national team. Ronaldo finished with 146 for Portugal, a total built over more than two decades that he kept growing until his final World Cup, where he scored his last international goal from the penalty spot against Croatia in the round of 32. The record has been his since 2021, when two goals against the Republic of Ireland took him to 111 and past Iran’s Ali Daei, who held it with 109.



The gap he leaves is enormous. Lionel Messi, the closest player on the list, ended his Argentina career with 126 goals, 20 fewer than Ronaldo, and since he retired in October after his farewell match against Benin, that total will not grow. Daei is long retired, and so is India’s Sunil Chhetri, who sits fourth on the list with 95 goals.



That leaves the active players with a mountain to climb. Belgium’s Romelu Lukaku, 33, has 94 goals and Poland’s Robert Lewandowski, 38, has 92, which puts both more than 50 goals short of Ronaldo. Given their ages, it is hard to imagine either of them catching up, and no one else is close enough to threaten the record.




Uma história que fica para sempre. 𝙊𝙗𝙧𝙞𝙜𝙖𝙙𝙤 𝙥𝙤𝙧 𝙩𝙪𝙙𝙤, 𝘾𝙖𝙥𝙞𝙩𝙖̃𝙤 🐐⭐️ pic.twitter.com/OSKr7L7xMW— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 5, 2026




234 caps: a mark that may be even harder to reach



The appearances record tells a similar story. Ronaldo finished with 234 caps for Portugal, a figure that makes him the most-capped player in the history of men’s international soccer. He broke the previous record of 196, held by Kuwait’s Bader Al-Mutawa, in 2023, and he was the first player to reach 200 appearances, a milestone he hit against Iceland in a Euro 2024 qualifier.


        


Behind him, the list is shorter on active players than it looks. Messi finished second with 208 caps, 26 fewer than Ronaldo, but he has already retired. The only name in the top five who could still add to his total is third-placed Luka Modric, with 206 caps for Croatia. At 41 years old, however, he would need more than 30 additional appearances to challenge Ronaldo, something that looks highly unlikely.



In the end, both records speak of the same thing: longevity and consistency at the highest level. To catch Ronaldo, a player would have to score at an elite rate and stay on the national team for more than two decades, without serious injuries or a drop in form. 



With Messi, Daei and the rest of the list already gone, and the active names far behind, the numbers that Ronaldo leaves behind, 146 goals and 234 caps, may stand for generations.

items.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
items.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeralThe narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente.The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. items.title: Argentina won’t use Lionel Messi’s No.10 jersey in the next window: Can they retire it for official competitions?
items.description:
With Lionel Messi gone, Argentina’s most iconic number has no owner for now, and head coach Lionel Scaloni has reportedly decided that no one will wear it in the next FIFA window. 
Argentina is preparing for a different kind of international window. Lionel Messi has stepped away from the national team after a farewell match against Benin, and with him goes the player who carried the most iconic number in Albiceleste history for two decades. The question now is what happens to the shirt he leaves behind, and whether it can be put away for good.



According to Argentine outlet TyC Sports, Messi’s No.10 will not be used by any other player in the upcoming international break. The decision was made by head coach Lionel Scaloni, who is waiting to pick the “next” number 10 for Argentina.



The gesture is possible because the November matches are friendlies, where FIFA does not require squads to use consecutive numbers. That allows Scaloni to leave the shirt untouched for now, a symbolic tribute to the player who retired as the national team’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.



The answer for official competition, however, is different. FIFA rules require World Cup and Copa America squad lists to use consecutive numbers from 1 to 26, with a number assigned to every player on the roster. That means Argentina cannot leave the No.10 unused or retire it for official tournaments, no matter how symbolic the gesture would be.



Lionel Messi #10 of Argentina during the 2026 World Cup. (Getty Images)



The Diego Maradona precedent



This is not the first time Argentina has run into this wall. Ahead of the 2002 World Cup, the AFA tried to retire the No.10 as a tribute to Diego Maradona, whose career had already turned the shirt into much more than a number. The federation even proposed a squad numbered up to 24 that would skip the No.10, but FIFA rejected the request, citing the consecutive-numbering rule.


        


As a result, the shirt kept being worn by later generations of Argentine players, with Ariel Ortega wearing it in 2002, until it eventually reached Messi. With the same regulation still in place, any renewed push to retire it in his honor would face the same outcome.



Who could inherit the No.10?



The bigger question will arrive when Argentina returns to official competition: who takes the shirt next? Nico Paz is the name most often mentioned, as the Como 1907 playmaker operates in a similar position to Messi and wears the same number at his club. The doubt is whether a 22-year-old can handle the weight of that number so early in his international career.



His performances this season suggest he can. Paz has been one of the standouts of the 2026-27 campaign, with six goals and eight assists in 13 appearances across Serie A and the UEFA Champions League.



Nico Paz celebrates a goal for Como 1907. (Getty Images)



Still, Argentina has other options. Some believe the shirt might be better suited to a proven World Cup winner, with Alexis Mac Allister, Julian Alvarez and Enzo Fernandez floated as alternatives who already have the pedigree and experience to carry that responsibility. For now, Scaloni appears in no rush: by leaving the shirt without an owner, he buys time before making one of the most symbolic decisions of the new era.

items.title: Matarazzo: "Europa exige más, claro, nos faltó ser más afilados, finos, precisos"
items.description: Matarazzo acabó el partido ante el Lyon con cierta rabia por no poder obtener tres puntos que cree firmemente que merecieron, y por alejarse además el objetivo del top 8 que no descarta en absoluto aún. "Hemos tenido un buen partido, especialmente la segunda parte con control y situaciones donde crear ocasiones. Faltó precisión en el pase final, no fue el mejor partido ofensivo hoy, sí bueno en lo defensivo. Los chicos compitieron muy bien 90 minutos. Defensivamente hemos invertido mucho tanto en la presión alta como en defender en bloque bajo. Hemos concedido muy fácil el gol, desafortunadamente. No han tenido muchas ocasiones, hay mucho positivo que sacar del partido. Queríamos los puntos hoy pero hay que seguir", dijo primero. Lamentó la falta de precisión en general. "El gol... no podemos conceder tan fácil. JonMa y Sergio, salta y no llega y no puedes hacerlo si no llegas. Tenemos que ser más precisos, finos, afilados para marcar más goles ante equipos así, teníamos espacios para atacar con números. Hemos tenido situaciones con Gonçalo recibiendo balón de portero en buena posición. Teníamos también mucho espacio entre sus centrales, que estaba estudiado, pero el pase iba muy despacio y no rompía. Tenemos que mejorar la toma de decisiones también para generar más".

items.title: Al Nassr pays tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo after his Portugal retirement: ‘Your name still echoes through our home’
items.description:
Al Nassr reacted to Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement from Portugal with a message that looks well beyond the goodbye. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s farewell to the Portugal national team did not go unnoticed in Saudi Arabia. Hours after the 41-year-old announced the end of his international career, Al Nassr made its voice heard.



The club shared the message on its official account on X, accompanied by an image of Ronaldo surrounded by his goal celebrations and the league trophy they won last season. “Your name still echoes through our home. Our ambitions still reach beyond the horizon and the story of Cristiano and Al Nassr still has the world turning pages,” the club wrote.



Ronaldo is still the face of Al Nassr’s project, and his time at the club is far from over. The forward signed a two-year extension in June 2025 that ties him to the team until mid-June 2027.



The Portuguese star is also firmly in the race to become the first player in history to reach 1,000 career goals, and everything points to him achieving it in Saudi Arabia. He currently sits at 985, after a hat trick in Al Nassr’s 5-3 win over Al Kholood, and he is the team’s top scorer this season with nine goals.




Your name still echoes through our homeOur ambitions still reach beyond the horizonAnd the story of @Cristiano and AlNassr still has the world turning pages 💛📜 pic.twitter.com/YqmzJLZ2hu— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) November 5, 2026




A story that is still being written



The club’s words also reflect how much the relationship has changed since Ronaldo arrived in early 2023. For more than three years, the Portuguese star went without an official title in Saudi Arabia, with his only trophy being the 2023 Arab Club Champions Cup, a tournament not officially recognized by FIFA. That wait ended in May 2026, when Al Nassr secured the 2025-26 Saudi Pro League crown with a 4-1 win over Damac, with Ronaldo scoring a brace.


        


Now, the challenge is to prove that the title was only the beginning. Al Nassr are trying to defend their crown this season and currently sit third in the Saudi Pro League with 28 points, two points behind leaders Al Hilal.



On the continental stage, Ronaldo is still chasing his first AFC Champions League Elite title with the club. Al Nassr are seventh in the West Region standings with six points from three matches, inside the qualification zone and with a game in hand over most of their rivals.



Now, with Portugal in the past, Al Nassr sees its captain as the center of a story that still has chapters to write. His contract runs through 2027, and nothing has been announced beyond that date, but the message from the club suggests that its ambitions, and his, are far from over.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from the Portugal national team: What is the future of his career with Al Nassr?
items.description:
After 23 years of carrying Portugal’s shirt, Cristiano Ronaldo has decided it is time to step away from the national team. The 41-year-old announced his retirement on Thursday, closing one of the most decorated international careers in football history. But the news does not mean the end of the road for the forward, who still […] 
After 23 years of carrying Portugal’s shirt, Cristiano Ronaldo has decided it is time to step away from the national team. The 41-year-old announced his retirement on Thursday, closing one of the most decorated international careers in football history.



But the news does not mean the end of the road for the forward, who still has unfinished business at club level in Saudi Arabia. Ronaldo remains under contract with Al Nassr, as he signed a two-year extension in 2025, keeping him in Riyadh until mid-June 2027.



That timeline gives the campaign extra weight, and Ronaldo seems to know it. Free from the demands of the national team, he arrives at this new stage in the best possible shape, fresh off a hat trick in Al Nassr’s 5-3 win over Al Kholood that took his career tally to 985 goals, just 15 away from the historic 1,000.



It was the perfect reminder that, at 41, his appetite for goals has not faded: he has scored nine times in 12 appearances this season, with eight of those goals coming in just 10 Saudi Pro League games and another in the AFC Champions League.




Portugal estará sempre em mim pic.twitter.com/dnFj51rxmh— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026




What could come after 2027?



How Ronaldo’s career ends is still an open question, and not even he seems to have the answer. Ahead of Portugal’s Nations League opener against Wales in September, the forward was asked directly about retirement and chose humor over clarity.


        


He admitted he simply does not know, explaining that since his early thirties he has lived in the moment rather than planning for tomorrow. He did not rule retirement out, acknowledging it was possible and even likely at some point, but refused to put a date on it.



What he did promise was how the news would arrive. When a reporter asked whether the Portuguese public would be the first to know, Ronaldo pushed back on the idea, saying: “I’ll tell the world, not just the Portuguese”.



The next question is about his club’s future. The forward could extend his stay at Al Nassr once more, look for a last challenge elsewhere or hang up his boots when his current contract expires. At the moment, nothing has been confirmed on any of those paths.



What does seem clear is that his retirement from Portugal frees up his schedule and his body. Without the long international breaks and the pressure of the national team, Ronaldo can focus fully on Al Nassr and on reaching the 1,000-goal mark.

items.title: AC Milan vs Ferencvaros: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for AC Milan vs Ferencvaros in the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League. AC Milan host Ferencvaros in the Europa League with momentum running in opposite directions heading into this one.
AC Milan come into this match off a rough patch, having lost 0-3 to Bournemouth on October 22 after a 4-0 win over Red Bull on October 15. The heavy defeat snapped the good feeling built by that rout, and it leaves Ruben Amorim needing a response in front of the home crowd. A win here would steady the ship after a result that exposed some issues at the back.
Ferencvaros arrive in form, having beaten Torreense 4-1 on October 22 on the back of a 2-1 win over Viktoria on October 15. Balázs Borbély’s side have strung together consecutive victories and look confident going forward. Another positive result in Milan would mark a significant statement for the Hungarian club’s European campaign.
AC Milan confirmed lineup
Amorim sets up AC Milan in a 3-4-3, with Mario Gila, Koni De Winter and Sankhoun Diawara forming the back three in front of Lorenzo Torriani. Davide Bartesaghi and Omari Hutchinson provide the width as wing-backs, with Yunus Musah and Ardon Jashari holding the midfield. Christian Pulisic, Gonçalo Ramos and Alphadjo Cissé make up the front three, giving AC Milan plenty of attacking options to try to bounce back from the Bournemouth defeat. There are no listed absences, so Amorim has his full squad to choose from.
AC Milan confirmed starting XI (4-4-1-1): Lorenzo Torriani, Filippo Terracciano, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara, Davide Bartesaghi, Omari Hutchinson, Ardon Jashari, Adrien Rabiot, Yunus Musah, Alphadjo Cissé, Gonçalo Ramos. Coach: Ruben Amorim.
Ferencvaros confirmed lineup
Borbély lines Ferencvaros up in a 4-2-3-1, with Olivér Nagy, Mariano Gómez, Nathan Zohoré and Callum O’Dowda forming the back four ahead of Dániel István Radnóti. Ádám Nagy and Kristoffer Zachariassen sit as the double pivot, screening the defense and feeding the attacking trio of Ádám Madarász, Dániel Arzani and Yusuf Bamidele behind lone striker Veljko Birmančević. With no absences to account for, Borbély can field his strongest available lineup as Ferencvaros look to extend their winning run away from home.
Ferencvaros confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Dénes Dibusz, Attila Osváth, Mariano Gómez, Toon Raemaekers, Carlos Eduardo Lopes Cruz, Matúš Bero, Ádám Nagy, Márius Corbu, Kristoffer Zachariassen, Lenny Joseph, Veljko Birmančević. Coach: Balázs Borbély.

items.title: Why is Christian Pulisic not starting for Milan vs Ferencvaros in 2026-27 UEFA Europa League?
items.description:
As Ruben Amorim prepares his team for a crucial UEFA Europa League meeting with Ferencvaros, the Portuguese coach has opted for a different approach to his starting lineup. 
Christian Pulisic made a decisive contribution to Milan’s impressive derby victory over Inter, but his performance has not guaranteed him another starting appearance in the club’s next European fixture. As Ruben Amorim prepares his team for a crucial UEFA Europa League meeting with Ferencvaros, the Portuguese coach has opted for a different approach to his starting lineup.



The Rossoneri return to San Siro on Thursday, November 5, encouraged by their 3-1 win over their city rivals. However, the team still has considerable work to do in Europe, while its Hungarian opponent arrives with a perfect record after winning their opening three league-phase matches.



Milan enjoyed an excellent evening against Inter, claiming a 3-1 victory in the Derby della Madonnina. Pulisic opened the scoring, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira added to the advantage and helped Amorim’s side secure another important result against their city rivals.



However, the Rossoneri have struggled to reproduce that form in the Europa League. Defeats against Benfica and Bournemouth, with a 4-0 victory over Salzburg in between, have left the Italian side with just three points from their first three matches.









That return places Milan 24th in the league-phase standings, currently occupying the final play-off position. With five fixtures remaining, Amorim needs his players to deliver more consistent performances to avoid making their route towards the knockout stages unnecessarily difficult.



Ferencvaros arrives with impressive European record



Ferencvaros present a difficult challenge for Milan, having won all three of their Europa League matches so far. Victories over Celtic, Viktoria Plzen and Torreense have earned Balazs Borbely’s side nine points and a place among the competition’s leading teams, putting them in contention for direct qualification to the last 16.



Their domestic form has also been impressive, with the Hungarian club reportedly going 20 consecutive matches without defeat across all competitions. Kristoffer Zachariassen and Dele Yusuf have been particularly important in attack, while Veljko Birmancevic provides another threat in the final third.









Thursday’s encounter will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencvaros. The Italian club has faced Hungarian opposition in previous European campaigns, but the two teams have never played each other in a competitive fixture.



Why is Pulisic not starting against Ferencvaros?



Despite scoring against Inter, Pulisic will begin the Ferencvaros match on the bench, with Amorim preparing to rotate his squad following the derby and ahead of Sunday’s domestic trip to Genoa.



Ruben Amorim, Manager of AC Milan, interacts with Christian Pulisic of AC Milan



The decision appears to be tactical rather than related to the American’s performance or fitness. The Red and Blacks coach wants to distribute playing time across his squad, creating opportunities for younger players while preserving some regular starters for the demanding schedule ahead.



According to the official lineup, Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse will feature in the wide positions, with Rabiot operating behind Goncalo Ramos. Pulisic is therefore among the experienced players who could be introduced from the bench if the club needs a different attacking dimension during the game. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
items.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so longNothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye?The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

items.title: The international break is almost here: so wave goodbye to your players, and maybe your manager | Max Rushden
items.description: What used to be a time to reset is now a time to rehire, and Michael Carrick is not the only Premier League manager looking over his shoulderPerhaps the most telling moment of Manchester United’s comeback against Roma was at the final whistle. The camera focused on Michael Carrick, who shook the hand of Gian Piero Gasperini before looking around trying to remember what you’re meant to do after a victory. The camera then cut to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, clapping with two of the most ashen faces you could imagine – as if it was a minute’s applause in the 87th minute for a lifelong, octogenarian fan who died peacefully in his sleep earlier in the week (most probably not at a United game but you couldn’t rule it out).Of course, there are rules about smiling when you are involved with a failing football club. Players can’t be seen to be enjoying themselves in the week after a defeat, managers have to be earnest at almost all times, apart from when a journalist’s phone goes off at a press conference – a moment of sporting hilarity on a par with a pigeon landing on Centre Court. Cristiano Ronaldo has brought his remarkable international career with Portugal to an end, but his decision does not mean he is ready to walk away from soccer. The experienced forward is now turning his attention towards the remaining challenges of his club career, although an unexpected change to Al-Nassr’s schedule has complicated his immediate return to action.



The Portuguese superstar is approaching another important stage of his career, with his pursuit of 1,000 goals still unfinished. However, supporters will have to wait a little longer to see him back on the pitch after a recent fixture announcement in Saudi Arabia. Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5 through an emotional video shared on social media, ending a 23-year journey with Portugal. 



He finished with 234 appearances and 146 goals, holding the men’s world records for both international caps and goals. “The day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team. I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world,” he said.



His departure followed a disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus after being left on the bench against Norway during the previous international window. Ronaldo subsequently left the national team camp, but his retirement announcement confirmed that his international career was over.



Portugal estará sempre em mim pic.twitter.com/dnFj51rxmh— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026 



The forward will continue playing for Al-Nassr, where he remains under contract until June 2027. He is sitting on 985 career goals, leaving him 15 short of the historic 1,000-goal milestone.



Saudi Pro League postponement delays Al-Nassr’s return



Ronaldo’s next club appearance has been affected by a wider adjustment to the Saudi Pro League calendar. The league announced that all Matchweek 13 fixtures in the 2026-27 season would be postponed following changes to the schedule of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, which Saudi Arabia is due to host.



The continental tournament has been moved from its original January-February window to December 2027, prompting the league to review its domestic calendar. The Saudi Pro League confirmed that replacement dates would be announced after discussions with clubs and other relevant stakeholders. “New dates for Matchweek 13 will be announced once the review is complete and the updated calendar has been agreed in coordination with all relevant stakeholders,” the league stated.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



One of the affected fixtures is Al-Nassr’s scheduled meeting with Al-Hazem, which has been postponed without a confirmed replacement date. The change adds to Al-Nassr’s disrupted schedule, with previous matches against Al-Ahli and Al-Wasl also having been postponed.



When will Cristiano Ronaldo play again?



With his international retirement confirmed, Ronaldo will no longer be involved in Portugal’s upcoming Nations League fixtures against Denmark and Wales. His next scheduled opportunity to return to competitive action is therefore Al-Nassr’s Saudi Pro League meeting with Al-Qadsiah on November 20, 2026.



Ange Postecoglou team Manager of Al Nassr and Cristiano Ronaldo



The match is expected to take place at Al-Awwal Park, although the kick-off time remains unconfirmed. The 41-year-old’s availability has also yet to be officially established.



The postponement of the Al-Hazem fixture means the Portuguese forward would face an extended break before returning to club soccer. If no additional matches are arranged, the November 20 meeting with Al-Qadsiah will mark his next opportunity to take the field.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo with Portugal or Lionel Messi with Argentina: Who had the better international career? The numbers tell the story
items.description:
Both became record-breakers, lifted major trophies, and carried the expectations of millions of supporters, but their achievements offer an intriguing comparison when placed side by side. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi brought an extraordinary era of international soccer to an end in 2026, closing chapters that transformed Portugal and Argentina into two of the sport’s most closely followed national teams. Both became record-breakers, lifted major trophies, and carried the expectations of millions of supporters, but their achievements offer an intriguing comparison when placed side by side.



Ronaldo announced his retirement from Portugal in November, following a 23-year international career, while Messi had already played his final match for Argentina in October. Their departures leave behind two remarkable legacies, although the statistics reveal some important differences in how they made their mark.



Messi’s emotional farewell to Argentina



Messi’s final appearance for Argentina came on October 6, 2026, in a friendly against Benin at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires. La Albiceleste won 3-0, with the captain scoring a penalty and providing two assists before receiving an emotional farewell from supporters. The 39-year-old finished his international career with 208 appearances, 126 goals and 67 assists.



His 21-year journey included the 2022 World Cup, Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024, and the 2022 Finalissima. Messi also captained Argentina to the 2026 World Cup final, where the national team lost 1-0 to Spain after extra time. His departure marked the beginning of a new chapter under Lionel Scaloni, with the national team leaving him out of its November squad.









Ronaldo ends his 23-year Portugal career



Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, 2026, through a video message shared on social media. His final appearance for Portugal had come in a 1-0 victory over Wales, before a disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus accelerated his departure. “The day has come to return the number 7 shirt of the National Team of all of us. I never felt it was exclusively mine,” the nation’s captain said in his farewell message.



The 41-year-old leaves with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both men’s international records. He also captained Portugal to its first European Championship in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.



Portugal estará sempre em mim pic.twitter.com/dnFj51rxmh— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026 



Ronaldo vs. Messi: What do the international numbers show?



The statistical comparison highlights Ronaldo’s advantage in appearances and goals, while Messi finished with more assists and total goal contributions.

Ronaldo scored 20 more international goals and played 26 more matches than Messi. However, Messi recorded ten more goal contributions overall despite making fewer appearances, averaging approximately 0.93 goals or assists per match compared with Ronaldo’s 0.78.



TrophyCristiano RonaldoLionel MessiFIFA World Cup01 (2022)Continental (Euro / Copa America)1 (2016)2 (2021, 2024)UEFA Nations League / Finalissima2 (2019, 2025)1 (2022)Total Major Senior Trophies34Major international trophies



The difference becomes even clearer when looking at their major international honors. Messi won the 2022 World Cup, two Copa America titles and the 2022 Finalissima, while Ronaldo collected Euro 2016 and two Nations League trophies with Portugal.



MetricLionel Messi (Copa América)Cristiano Ronaldo (UEFA Euro)Tournaments Played7 (2007–2024)6 (2004–2024)Matches Played3930Goals Scored1414Assists187Titles Won2 (2021, 2024)1 (2016)Continental tournaments (Copa America vs UEFA Euro)



World Cup achievements separate their international stories



Messi’s World Cup record includes 21 goals and 12 assists in 34 appearances, alongside the 2022 triumph that completed his collection of major international honors. He also became the first player to win the World Cup Golden Ball twice.



World Cup MetricCristiano RonaldoLionel MessiTournaments Played6 (2006–2026)6 (2006–2026)Matches Played2734Goals Scored1121FIFA World Cup records



Ronaldo appeared at a record six different World Cups, scoring 11 goals in 27 matches. Although he never lifted the trophy, he made history by scoring at all six tournaments and helped Portugal reach the semi-finals in 2006.

Their careers therefore represent two different paths to international greatness. Ronaldo’s legacy is built around longevity, goalscoring records and Portugal’s first major senior trophies, while Messi’s includes greater overall goal contributions and the World Cup title.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi both bring an end to their legendary international careers, but their simultaneous FIFA break absence is not a first
items.description:
Their departures from Portugal and Argentina have arrived in the same era, creating an unusual moment for international soccer, although history shows that the two superstars have experienced a similar absence from the international stage before. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have finally brought an end to two extraordinary international careers, marking a major turning point for soccer after more than two decades of defining the sport. Their departures from Portugal and Argentina have arrived in the same era, creating an unusual moment for international soccer. However, history shows that the two superstars have experienced a similar absence from the international stage before.



Ronaldo confirmed his retirement through an emotional video shared on social media, while Messi‘s departure had already been followed by Argentina’s first squad announcement without its legendary captain. Their exits leave two national teams preparing for the future without the players who became their greatest goalscorers and most recognizable figures.



Ronaldo announced his retirement from Portugal after 23 years, bringing an end to a career that began with his senior debut in 2003. The 41-year-old finished with 234 appearances and 146 goals, records that place him at the top of men’s international soccer in both categories. In his five-minute farewell video, titled OBRIGADO, PORTUGAL [THANK YOU, PORTUGAL], the veteran reflected on the responsibility of wearing the famous number seven shirt.



“To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team. I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.” He also expressed his pride in representing the Selecao, adding: “The number 7 shirt will remain. The pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me.”



Portugal estará sempre em mim pic.twitter.com/dnFj51rxmh— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026 



Meanwhile, Messi’s international career with Argentina also ended after more than two decades. He retired with 208 appearances, 126 goals and 69 assists, having won the 2022 World Cup, the 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles, and the 2022 Finalissima. La Albiceleste captain’s final appearance came in a farewell friendly against Benin, where he scored a penalty and provided two assists in a 3-0 victory. Like Ronaldo, Messi leaves behind a record that will be difficult for the next generation to approach.



Lionel Messi of Argentina celebrates his final international game



Duo previously disappeared from international play together



Despite the significance of their retirements, this is not the first time Ronaldo and Messi have been absent from international soccer during the same period. Following the 2018 World Cup in Russia, both players stepped away from their respective national teams for the remainder of the calendar year, as confirmed by The Mirror.



Their departures from that tournament happened on June 30, 2018, when Argentina and Portugal were both eliminated in the Round of 16. France defeated Argentina 4-3, while Uruguay knocked out Portugal with a 2-1 victory, leaving both superstars facing an early end to their World Cup campaigns.



Cristiano Ronaldo (left) and Lionel Messi (right) at the 2018 World Cup



Neither player returned for the September, October or November international windows. Both missed six matches for their countries before making their comebacks on March 22, 2019, bringing an unusual period of simultaneous absence to an end.



Their returns did not produce the results supporters had hoped for. Portugal drew 0-0 with Ukraine in a European qualifier, while Argentina lost 3-1 to Venezuela in a friendly, with Messi subsequently missing the next match through injury.



New international era begins without soccer’s defining duo



The latest departures carry greater significance because they appear to close the international careers of two players who dominated world soccer for an entire generation. Between 2008 and 2023, Ronaldo and Messi won 13 of the 15 Ballon d’Or awards, maintaining an extraordinary level of individual success alongside their international achievements.



2015 FIFA Ballon d’Or nominees Lionel Messi (L) and Cristiano Ronaldo (R)



Argentina has already begun preparing for life without Messi, announcing a 28-player squad for November friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica. Portugal must now move forward without Ronaldo as Jorge Jesus prepares to build a team around the players who will lead the next chapter.



Both superstars continue their club careers, with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr and Messi at Inter Miami. Their international journeys, however, have reached their conclusions, leaving behind records, trophies, and memories that will remain central to soccer history for years to come.

items.title: Kylian Mbappe joins Cristiano Ronaldo in an exclusive Real Madrid Champions League club with goal vs AEK Athens
items.description:
Kylian Mbappe scored again in the Champions League, and his streak has put him alongside Cristiano Ronaldo in an exclusive club at Real Madrid, though catching the Portuguese star’s mark will not be easy. 
Whenever a Real Madrid forward starts to pile up goals in the Champions League, the comparison with Cristiano Ronaldo is never far behind. The Portuguese star left a standard in the competition that few players have come close to touching, and Kylian Mbappe has now put himself in a conversation that, until this week, had only one name in it.



Mbappe scored in his sixth consecutive Champions League match, which ties the best streak of his career, set with PSG in 2022. The run includes goals against Bayern Munich (twice), Inter, Roma, Leipzig and now AEK Athens.



Until now, only one Real Madrid player had scored in six or more consecutive matches in the history of the competition: Ronaldo, who did it in 11 straight matches, from the final in Cardiff in 2017 until April 2018.



With six matches in a row, Mbappe is now five away from tying Ronaldo’s mark of 11, a streak that will be hard to match. The Frenchman is also having a standout season in general, with 16 goals and three assists in 15 matches across LaLiga and the Champions League. 




🔟 @KMbappe 🔟 pic.twitter.com/agSXQRYED2— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) November 4, 2026




In Spain, he has scored 12 goals in 11 matches, while in Europe he has scored in all four of Real Madrid’s matches, for four goals and one assist. Each match gives him a new chance to extend a run that has already earned him a place beside one of the club’s greatest legends.



Mbappe’s path to catching Cristiano Ronaldo


        


To equal Ronaldo’s mark of 11, Mbappe needs to score in five more consecutive Champions League matches, and the schedule gives him four chances in the league phase. 



According to Real Madrid’s official schedule, Real Madrid host PSV in Matchday 5, visit Arsenal, last season’s runner-up, in Matchday 6, host LASK in Matchday 7, and close the phase against Shakhtar Donetsk on Jan. 27 in London, the city where the Ukrainian side plays its Champions League home matches.



After that, Real Madrid, who have won all four of their league-phase matches so far, will move on to the knockout phase, and that is where the streak would be decided.



In this way, the league phase alone would not be enough for Mbappe to catch Cristiano. Even if he scores in each of Real Madrid’s four remaining matches, he would reach 10 consecutive games with a goal, one short of the Portuguese star’s 11. The knockout phase will have the final word, and only a goal in the first match of that stage would put the Frenchman level with one of the club’s greatest legends.

items.title: Christian Pulisic learns Ruben Amorim’s selection decision ahead of Milan’s UEFA Europa League test vs Ferencvaros after Inter heroics
items.description:
With Ruben Amorim preparing his side for a crucial UEFA Europa League encounter against Ferencvaros, the Portuguese coach is considering several changes as Milan attempts to recover from a disappointing start to their continental campaign. 
Christian Pulisic made a decisive contribution to Milan’s derby victory over Inter, but it remains to be seen whether his impressive performance guarantees another starting appearance in the club’s next European fixture. With Ruben Amorim preparing his side for a crucial UEFA Europa League encounter against Ferencvaros, the Portuguese coach is considering several changes as Milan attempts to recover from a disappointing start to their continental campaign.



The Rossoneri return to San Siro encouraged by their latest domestic result, although their European position leaves little room for another setback. Ferencvaros, meanwhile, arrive in Italy with a perfect record after winning their opening three league-phase matches.



Milan produced an impressive display against Inter at the weekend, securing a 3-1 victory in the Derby della Madonnina. Pulisic opened the scoring, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira added to the advantage and helped Amorim’s side claim another important result against their city rivals.



However, the Rossoneri have struggled to reproduce that form in the Europa League. Defeats against Benfica and Bournemouth, with a 4-0 victory over Salzburg in between, have left the Italian side with three points from their opening three matches.



ClubMatchday 1 ResultMatchday 2 ResultMatchday 3 ResultRecord (W-D-L)PointsTable RankMilanLoss 0–2 vs Benfica (H)Win 4–0 Salzburg (A)Loss 0–3 Bournemouth (A)1–0–2324thFerencvarosWin 3–1 Celtic (A)Win 2–1 vs Viktoria Plzen (H)Win 4–1 vs Torreense (H)3–0–095th



That return places Milan 24th in the league-phase standings, occupying the final play-off position. With five fixtures remaining, Amorim needs his players to deliver more consistent performances if the club is to avoid an unnecessarily difficult route towards the knockout stages.



Ferencvaros arrive with impressive European record



Ferencvaros present a difficult challenge for Milan, having won all three of their Europa League matches so far. Victories over Celtic, Viktoria Plzen and Torreense have put the Hungarian side on nine points and fifth place in the standings, giving Balazs Borbely’s team a genuine opportunity to qualify directly for the last 16.



Their domestic form has also been impressive. The Greens have reportedly gone 20 consecutive matches without defeat across all competitions, while their recent attacking performances have made them one of the most dangerous sides in the competition.



Five teams remain with a 100% winning record 😤

#UEL https://t.co/aDRNhGHsks— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) November 3, 2026



Thursday’s encounter will be the first competitive meeting between the two sides. The Italian giants previously faced Hungarian opposition in European competition, meeting Gyori in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup and Szombathelyi Haladas in the 1982 Mitropa Cup.



Will Pulisic feature against Ferencvaros?



Despite scoring against Inter, Pulisic is expected to be among the substitutes when Milan faces Ferencvaros. Amorim is preparing to rotate his squad after the derby and ahead of the upcoming domestic fixture against Genoa, with several younger players in contention for opportunities.



MilanNews’ predicted starting XI suggests that Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse could feature in the wide positions, while Adrien Rabiot is expected to operate behind Goncalo Ramos. Francesco Camarda is another option in attack, although Ramos appears to be the preferred choice to lead the line.



Christian Pulisic of AC Milan



Pulisic’s expected absence from the starting XI would therefore appear to be a selection decision rather than a consequence of his performance against Inter. His contribution in the derby has strengthened his case for regular involvement, but Amorim has other priorities as he manages the squad across multiple competitions.



Milan will also have to cope with several absences. Mike Maignan is suspended following his red card against Bournemouth, meaning Lorenzo Torriani is expected to start in goal, while Fikayo Tomori, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze remain unavailable.

items.title: Christian Pulisic learns his USMNT fate as Mauricio Pochettino recalls three familiar faces for CONCACAF Nations League’s Haiti clashes
items.description:
Christian Pulisic's international future has become a talking point ahead of the United States men's national team's return to competitive action, with Mauricio Pochettino preparing a squad that blends established stars and emerging talent 
Christian Pulisic‘s international future has become a talking point ahead of the United States men’s national team’s return to competitive action, with Mauricio Pochettino preparing a squad that blends established stars and emerging talent. The November selection also brings back three familiar faces who missed the previous international window, as the USMNT prepares for a crucial CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti.



The two-legged tie will mark the team’s first competitive assignment since its disappointing World Cup exit against Belgium. Pochettino will be looking to build on the momentum generated by four consecutive victories in September and October while continuing to shape his squad for the next World Cup cycle.



Pochettino announced a 25-player roster on Wednesday, with Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie among the most notable returnees. They missed the previous international window, during which the United States defeated Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.



Balogun returns after a difficult few months involving his World Cup suspension controversy and a failed transfer to Everton. The Monaco striker struggled for regular minutes at the beginning of the season but has recently featured more consistently, giving the manager another attacking option.



Christian Pulisic #10 and Weston McKennie #8 of the United States celebrate a goal.



McKennie, meanwhile, missed the previous camp because of fatigue and is back after returning to regular involvement with Juventus. Their inclusion gives the United States three experienced players who could prove important in the knockout tie against Haiti.



Has Pulisic received his international recall?



The biggest question surrounding Pulisic has now been answered, with the Milan forward included in Pochettino’s 25-man squad for the November fixtures. His return is particularly significant after missing four consecutive friendlies while recovering from the injury he sustained at the World Cup.



Pulisic’s absence came while he recovered from a serious lower-leg injury sustained during the World Cup’s round-of-16 defeat against Belgium. The Milan forward suffered a microfracture involving his right tibia and fibula but has since returned to action at club level.



Right back into it in Red White & Blue. 🇺🇸

Mauricio Pochettino has called in 25 players for our November camp and pair of @CNationsLeague quarterfinal matches against Haiti!

#USMNT x @ouraring https://t.co/qwZu0R9J23— U.S. Soccer Men’s National Team (@USMNT) November 4, 2026



The 28-year-old forward has gradually regained his fitness and form with the Rossoneri, making his return to the national team an important step ahead of the next international cycle. However, competition for places in Pochettino’s attack remains strong, with Balogun joining Justin Ellis, Julian Hall and Cavan Sullivan among the selected forwards.



Pochettino has also stressed the importance of creating competition within the squad rather than relying exclusively on familiar names. “It’s very important for us to add more options, more players with the possibility to challenge the familiar faces,” the coach said during an online news conference.



Christian Pulisic #10 of the United States react after the FIFA World Cup 2026.



United States prepares for two matches against Haiti



The United States will face Haiti twice in the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals, with the first meeting scheduled for November 14 in Miami. Although Haiti is officially the home team, ongoing security concerns in the Caribbean nation mean the match will take place at Nu Stadium.



The return fixture will be played on November 17 at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati, with the aggregate winner advancing to the Nations League semifinals in March 2027. The winner will also secure automatic qualification for the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup.

items.title: Why is Federico Valverde not starting for Real Madrid vs AEK Athens in the 2026-27 Champions League?
items.description:
Real Madrid visit AEK Athens in Matchday 4 of the 2026-27 Champions League, and the big surprise is that captain Federico Valverde is not among the starters. Manager Jose Mourinho has left the Uruguayan midfielder on the bench in the club’s confirmed lineup, and Denzel Dumfries has been chosen to take his place on the […] 
Real Madrid visit AEK Athens in Matchday 4 of the 2026-27 Champions League, and the big surprise is that captain Federico Valverde is not among the starters. Manager Jose Mourinho has left the Uruguayan midfielder on the bench in the club’s confirmed lineup, and Denzel Dumfries has been chosen to take his place on the right side of the defense.



The most likely reason is physical. Valverde felt discomfort in the first half of Real Madrid’s win over Barcelona in the Clasico and came off in the second half. Initial assessments ruled out a serious injury, but he was unable to train normally with the squad and missed the 3-0 win over Racing Santander, as the coaching staff decided against risking him.



The decision also fits with how the week was managed. Valverde returned to training with the first team on Nov. 2, so the Portuguese manager decided not to risk him from the start of the match.



Mourinho made it clear before the match that the absence has nothing to do with a lack of confidence in him. “I see Fede as an extremely important player for the team,” the manager said, adding that being captain makes him look at things differently and that he would play wherever the team needs him.




📋✅ ¡Nuestro XI inicial!🆚 @AEK_FC_OFFICIAL pic.twitter.com/gM6aRRCI7s— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) November 4, 2026




Valverde has been used as the preferred right-back in recent matches, but Trent Alexander-Arnold played the full game in that position against Racing. Both are available from the bench against AEK.



Real Madrid’s confirmed lineup


        


Mourinho has confirmed his XI for the match in Athens, with Vinicius Junior wearing the captain’s armband in Valverde’s absence. Real Madrid’s starting XI: Courtois, Dumfries, Militao, Rudiger, Cucurella, Camavinga, Bernardo, Bellingham, Yan Diomande, Vinicius Junior (C), Mbappe.



The bench includes Valverde, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Endrick, Brahim, Thiago, Huijsen, Konate and Carreras, along with goalkeeper Lunin and youngsters Mestre, Espi and Sergio Martinez.



With Valverde’s status uncertain, Mourinho has the captain available if the match requires him. Real Madrid want to keep their perfect record in the Champions League after winning all three of their matches so far, and the priority is clear: take three more points in Athens while making sure the Uruguayan arrives healthy for the stretch of matches ahead.

items.title: Fenerbahce vs Liverpool: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Fenerbahce vs Liverpool in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Fenerbahce host Liverpool in the Champions League with the home side looking to settle an uneven run while the visitors bring one of the competition’s most potent attacks to Istanbul.
Fenerbahce drew 2-2 with Slavia Praha on October 20 after being routed 0-6 by Aston Villa on October 14. The heavy defeat to Villa exposed problems at the back that the draw with Slavia only partly eased. Dirk Kuyt needs a result here to steady confidence before the group stage tightens.
Liverpool won 4-3 against Villarreal on October 20 and followed an even higher-scoring 6-3 win over LASK on October 14. Both matches came with goals conceded as well as scored, suggesting an attack-first approach under Andoni Iraola. A win in Istanbul would keep Liverpool firmly on track in the competition.
Fenerbahce confirmed lineup
Kuyt sets Fenerbahce up in a 4-2-3-1 with Ederson behind a back four of Müldür, Škriniar, Brown and Mercan. Guendouzi and Kanté sit as the double pivot, giving the side some control and experience in midfield, while Kahveci, Greenwood and Aydin support Lukaku as the central striker. There are no absences to account for, so Kuyt can pick his strongest available group, though the shape will need to hold up better defensively than it did against Aston Villa.
Fenerbahce confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Ederson, Nélson Semedo, Archie Brown, N’Golo Kanté, Milan Škriniar, Kojo Peprah Oppong, Mattéo Guendouzi, İsmail Yüksek, Romelu Lukaku, Mason Greenwood, İrfan Can Kahveci. Coach: Dirk Kuijt.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Iraola fields Liverpool in a matching 4-2-3-1, with Alisson in goal behind Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk and Tsimikas across the back line. Nyoni and Mac Allister anchor midfield, feeding Wirtz, Barcola and Ngumoha behind lone striker Gakpo. With no absences listed, Iraola can call on his first-choice attacking group, and the balance of that front four suggests Liverpool will again look to win the game by scoring more than they concede.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo has last laugh as his 2017-18 record remains UEFA Champions League benchmark after Harry Kane misses chance to rewrite history
items.description:
The English striker helped his team secure an important victory against Atletico Madrid, although the evening carried a different significance for Cristiano Ronaldo and his place in European soccer history. 
Harry Kane came close to reaching another extraordinary milestone in the UEFA Champions League, but his latest appearance for Bayern Munich ended with an unexpected personal disappointment. The English striker helped his team secure an important victory against Atletico Madrid, although the evening carried a different significance for Cristiano Ronaldo and his place in European soccer history. A long-standing record from the Portuguese superstar’s Real Madrid days has survived another serious challenge.



Bayern travelled to Madrid looking to strengthen their position in the Champions League league phase, while Atletico hoped to use their home advantage to secure a valuable result. Instead, the German side produced a disciplined performance to claim a 2-0 victory, with Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer scoring the decisive goals.



Kane did not find the net, bringing an impressive European scoring sequence to an end. However, the Bayern forward still played an important role by providing the assist for Laimer’s second-half strike, helping his team collect all three points.



The result was particularly encouraging for the Bavarians after a frustrating 2-2 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga. The 33-year-old Ballon d’Or winner had also endured a difficult individual performance in that match, missing a penalty and hitting the crossbar.









Cristiano Ronaldo’s Champions League record remains untouched



Kane entered the Atletico encounter having scored in 10 consecutive Champions League appearances, putting him within reach of one of the competition’s most remarkable individual records. A goal against Simeone’s team would have allowed him to equal Ronaldo’s benchmark of scoring in 11 successive matches.



However, the Englishman was unable to extend his streak, meaning Ronaldo remains the only player to have scored in 11 consecutive Champions League games. The Portuguese forward established the record with Real Madrid during the 2017-18 campaign, when the Spanish club went on to win its third consecutive European title.



Players that have scored in the most consecutive Champions League games: 

◉ 11 – Cristiano Ronaldo (2017/18) 
◎ 10 – Harry Kane (2026)

Harry Kane falls one game short of equalling CR7’s record. 👀 https://t.co/Bq0y05XyVn— Squawka (@Squawka) November 3, 2026




Ronaldo’s remarkable sequence began with a brace against Juventus in the 2017 Champions League final. He subsequently scored in all six group-stage matches before finding the net in both legs of Real Madrid’s round-of-16 and quarter-final ties.



His run eventually ended against Bayern Munich in the semi-finals, when he failed to score. Nevertheless, Real Madrid progressed and later defeated Liverpool in the final to complete another memorable European campaign.



How Harry Kane built his 10-match scoring streak



Kane’s pursuit of Ronaldo’s record began during the 2025-26 Champions League campaign. He scored twice against Union Saint-Gilloise before finding the net against PSV in his following appearance.



The England international then continued his impressive run after returning to the starting lineup against Atalanta, scoring twice in the second leg of Bayern’s round-of-16 tie. He subsequently scored in every European appearance until Bayern’s campaign ended against Paris Saint-Germain in the semi-finals.



RankPlayerClubSeasonConsecutive games1.Cristiano RonaldoReal Madrid2017–18112.Harry KaneBayern2026–present103.Ruud van NistelrooyManchester United2002–0393.Robert LewandowskiBayern2019–2093.Robert LewandowskiBayern2020–2196.Cristiano RonaldoReal Madrid2013–148



The Englishman carried that momentum into the current season, scoring against Bodo/Glimt, Viking FK and Arsenal. His penalty against Arsenal on matchday three took his streak to 10 consecutive matches, leaving him just one goal away from matching Ronaldo.



Despite missing out against Atletico, Kane remains second on the all-time list, ahead of Ruud van Nistelrooy and Robert Lewandowski, who each recorded scoring streaks of nine consecutive Champions League appearances.

items.title: ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham
items.description: WSL’s second-highest goalscorer is likened to England legend for her crossing and has earned France call-upAt the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. It was an innocuous moment that might have escaped most onlookers at Hednesford Town’s Keys Park but it demonstrated the swagger with which she is playing.To observe the 22-year-old warming up before the 1-1 League Cup draw at Aston Villa last week was to witness a player making skills look easy, taking one touch where others took two and pulling off no-look passes. She is backing up that panache in the Women’s Super League, as the joint second-highest goalscorer with six from the promoted side’s opening eight matches. Only Khadija Shaw has scored more. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s mysterious ‘M’ hand gesture celebration sparks an intriguing theory among fans
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been making a mysterious ‘M’ hand gesture, and fans believe it could be linked to his chase for 1,000 career goals. 
Few players generate as much attention for their celebrations as Cristiano Ronaldo, and the Al Nassr forward has given fans something new to talk about. Over recent weeks, he has been seen repeating a particular gesture that has sparked curiosity on social media, where supporters are trying to work out whether it carries a hidden message.



Ronaldo has been spotted making an “M” with his fingers after scoring for Al Nassr lately, although nobody knows exactly what it means. The gesture has no official explanation, and the player has not publicly addressed it, so the interpretations so far come from fans.



According to the sports social media account 433, the most popular theory is that the “M” stands for 1,000, since it is the Roman numeral for that number. The idea makes sense given the context: Ronaldo is chasing a historic milestone of 1,000 career goals, a number he has described in the past as one of his biggest objectives.



For now, the meaning of the gesture remains an open question, and only Ronaldo can confirm whether the theory is correct, along with perhaps Al Nassr CEO Jose Semedo, who has also celebrated with the Portuguese star using the same gesture.




فيه احد عرف المقصد ؟ 😂 https://t.co/OTlLFRkdfp pic.twitter.com/Ombs0bAWgz— نادي النصر السعودي (@AlNassrFC) October 23, 2026




What is certain is that each goal he scores brings him closer to a number no player in football history has reached, and fans will be watching closely to see if the “M” appears again when the milestone gets closer.



Can Cristiano reach 1,000 career goals before 2026 ends?


        


Ronaldo currently has 985 career goals, which leaves him 15 away from the historic mark. Reaching it before the end of the year does not look like an easy task for the Portuguese striker, who has eight matches left in 2026 after the 6-2 win over Pakhtakor. That count does not include the match against Al Hazem, which was postponed and has no new date yet.



In the Saudi Pro League, he will play five matches against Al Qadsiah, Al Shabab, Al-Fayha, Al Hilal and Al-Fateh, while Al Nassr will also face Al Kholood in a King’s Cup tie on Dec. 1.



In international competition, Al Nassr have two AFC Champions League Elite matches, against Al Sadd and Al-Gharafa. If the team qualifies for the knockout round, those matches would be played from 2027.



With eight matches left and 15 goals needed, scoring only one goal per game would not be enough for Ronaldo. However, if the Al Hazem match is rescheduled before the end of the year, he would have one more chance to add to his tally. And if he does not reach the legendary mark in 2026, he will likely finish close enough to get there in the first days of 2027.

items.title: Why is Vincent Kompany not on the bench for Bayern Munich vs Atletico Madrid today in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League?
items.description:
Vincent Kompany will not be in the dugout at the Metropolitano, leaving his assistant to take charge against Diego Simeone's team. His absence comes at a particularly demanding moment for Bayern, who are also dealing with several injury problems. 
Bayern Munich faces a difficult Champions League test against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, November 3, but the German side will have to manage the challenge without an important figure on the touchline. Vincent Kompany will not be in the dugout at the Metropolitano, leaving his assistant to take charge against Diego Simeone’s team. His absence comes at a particularly demanding moment for Bayern, who are also dealing with several injury problems.



The Champions League encounter represents an important opportunity for both clubs as they look to improve their positions in the league phase. Bayern entered the match with five points from their opening three games, while Atletico Madrid had collected four, making the result particularly significant for their ambitions of reaching the knockout rounds.



Atleti have the advantage of playing at home, where Simeone’s team have been particularly difficult to beat. The Spanish side have also enjoyed an impressive run of domestic results, including seven consecutive La Liga victories and a 2-0 win over Levante in their most recent outing.



Bayern, meanwhile, arrive in Madrid after a 2-2 draw against Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker. The German side have also shared the points with Arsenal and Viking FK in their previous Champions League fixtures, making Tuesday’s match another demanding test.



MatchdayBayern ResultsAtletico Madrid ResultsMatchday 1W 5–0 vs. Bodo/Glimt (H)L 2–1 vs. Liverpool (A)Matchday 2D 3–3 vs. Viking (A)W 2–0 vs. Manchester United (H)Matchday 3D 2–2 vs. Arsenal (H)D 1–1 vs. Stuttgart (A)



Why is Vincent Kompany missing against Atletico Madrid?



The reason for Kompany’s absence is a health issue that forced him to step away from his managerial responsibilities in late October. The Bayern coach collapsed during a training session involving the club’s reserve team on October 23 and was subsequently taken to hospital.



Following medical examinations, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl confirmed that Kompany had been diagnosed with meningeal irritation. The condition involves irritation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, requiring the Belgian coach to rest and receive treatment.



🚨 Bayern club statement on Vincent Kompany health conditions.

Vincent Kompany had to receive medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session of FC Bayern’s second team. The first-team head coach had been watching the second team’s training session. Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical supervision. Until further notice, his coaching staff will take charge of training and matchday operations.

Max Eberl: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure that he recovers quickly. Vinnie will receive all the necessary medical care and support, as well as all the time he needs. His coaching staff, whom we trust completely, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery.”— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) October 23, 2026




Kompany was discharged from hospital on October 28 and has continued his recovery at home. However, Bayern have taken a cautious approach, making it clear that his return to the dugout will depend on his health rather than a fixed deadline.



The club has also instructed its coaching staff to avoid discussing football matters with him during his recovery. The intention is to ensure that Kompany can concentrate on his health and family without worrying about tactics, team selections or upcoming matches.



When will Kompany return to Bayern’s bench?



With Kompany unavailable, assistant coach Aaron Danks will lead Bayern from the touchline against Atletico. The Englishman is not taking over as the club’s permanent manager, but has been entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing the team until Kompany is ready to return.



Manuel Neuer alongside Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompan



The Bavarians have not provided an exact date for Kompany’s return, although reports indicate that he is unlikely to resume his touchline duties before the November international break. The Belgian is expected to miss the Champions League clash against Atletico, as well as the Bundesliga matches against Borussia Dortmund and Mainz.



According to BILD, Kompany will continue his rest and treatment during the international break, with a return potentially coming later in November. Bayern’s next scheduled Bundesliga fixture after the break is against Cologne on November 20, although his availability for that match will depend on his recovery.

items.title: Manchester United vs Roma: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Manchester United vs Roma in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Manchester United host Roma at a time when both clubs need a Champions League result to settle some nerves, and the contrast in how they arrive here gives this fixture its edge.
Manchester United come into this one on a two-game skid, having lost 1-4 to Como 1907 on October 21 after a 0-2 defeat to Atlético on October 13. Those two results have piled pressure on Michael Carrick, and the goals conceded in bunches point to problems at the back that have not been fixed. A win here would steady the ship, while another loss would deepen the concern around this group.
Roma arrive in better shape, having bounced back from a 3-4 loss to Real Madrid on October 14 with a 4-0 win over Slovan on October 20. That victory showed Gian Piero Gasperini’s side can still score freely when things click going forward. Taking points off United would mark real progress in their European campaign and answer any doubts left by the Madrid defeat.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Carrick sets United up in a 4-2-3-1, with Dalot and Mazraoui as the full-backs either side of Maguire and Martínez at center-back. Tielemans and Mainoo sit in a double pivot screening the defense, while Bruno Fernandes gets license to roam behind Mbeumo, Mount and Cunha in a fluid front four built around Mbeumo’s pace on the right. There are no absences to work around, so this is as close to a first-choice group as Carrick can put out, which makes the recent defensive form harder to explain away.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Senne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Diogo Dalot, Carlos Baleba, Harry Maguire, Ayden Heaven, Bryan Mbeumo, Kobbie Mainoo, Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Amad Diallo. Coach: Michael Carrick.
Roma confirmed lineup
Gasperini goes with his trusted 3-4-2-1, built on a back three of Ndicka, Mancini and Hermoso shielding goalkeeper Vásquez. Molina and Wesley França provide width as wing-backs, with Cristante and De Roon controlling the center of the pitch, and Pisilli given a free role just behind the front line. Soulé and Malen support central striker Malen’s spearhead role, giving Roma the same attacking pattern that produced the win over Slovan. With a clean bill of health, Gasperini can call on his first-choice XI to try to disrupt United at Old Trafford.
Roma confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Devis Vásquez, Devyne Rensch, Wesley, Mario Hermoso, Leonardo Balerdi, Gianluca Mancini, Bryan Cristante, Marten de Roon, Donyell Malen, Rodrigo Mora, Matías Soulé. Coach: Gian Piero Gasperini.

items.title: Why are Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia not playing for PSG vs Villarreal in 2026-27 UEFA Champions League?
items.description:
PSG will be without Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia against Villarreal, with a muscle injury for one and a torn cruciate ligament for the other. 
Paris Saint-Germain head to Spain for Matchday 4 of the Champions League as the reigning European champions, riding a long winning streak and leading the league phase. But the trip to Villarreal comes with a notable handicap: two of the club’s most dangerous attackers are not part of the plan, and their absences have changed the way Luis Enrique can set up his front line.



Both injuries took place in the same match. During PSG’s 4-2 win over Barcelona in Matchday 3, Ousmane Dembele pulled up in the 19th minute while sprinting and grabbed his left thigh, with the club’s medical staff later pointing to a muscle injury.



He had been in outstanding form, with four goals and six assists in ten competitive matches this season, including six goal contributions in just two Champions League games.



On the other hand, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered a more serious blow in the same game. After almost an hour, the Georgian twisted his knee in a fair challenge by Barcelona’s Xavi Espart and landed awkwardly on the turf, needing help to leave the pitch. PSG later confirmed that he has torn his cruciate ligament, an injury that will keep him out for months, and he is still recovering.




⚽️ Jour de Ligue des champions !#UCL pic.twitter.com/1X4UfX6KtC— Paris Saint-Germain (@PSG_inside) November 3, 2026




A long injury list for Luis Enrique



Dembele and Kvaratskhelia are not the only absences for PSG. Captain Marquinhos, who also went off injured against Barcelona, is missing with a hamstring strain, while Nuno Mendes and Alessandro Longoni are out with leg injuries. The list leaves Luis Enrique with fewer options on the wings and in defense than he would like.


        


Even so, the French club has the depth to keep competing at the top. The preview expects Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Desire Doue to lead the attack, while Achraf Hakimi, who scored a hat trick in the 5-1 win over Le Havre, arrives in strong form on the right side.



With so many players unavailable, PSG will need their depth to make the difference at Estadio de la Ceramica. Luis Enrique’s side has shown this season that it can win with different faces, and Villarreal, who have struggled for consistency, will try to take advantage of a team that is missing some of its biggest names.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s son gets first Portugal U-17 call-up as possible debut date emerges after family timeline reveals striking coincidence
items.description:
The selection has brought renewed attention to the teenager’s international progress, with an intriguing connection between the two generations adding another layer of interest to his upcoming opportunity. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s son is taking another significant step towards following his father’s path after earning his first call-up to Portugal’s Under-17 national team. The selection has brought renewed attention to the teenager’s international progress, with an intriguing connection between the two generations adding another layer of interest to his upcoming opportunity.



Cristiano Ronaldo Jr., 16, has been included in head coach Filipe Ramos’ 23-man squad for the opening round of qualifying matches for the 2027 UEFA European Under-17 Championship. The Al-Nassr academy forward has already represented Portugal at Under-15 and Under-16 level, but this promotion marks another important milestone in his development.



The teenager has gradually worked his way through Portugal’s youth system since making his international debut in May 2025. He has recorded 13 appearances and five goals across the Under-15 and Under-16 teams, scoring twice in four matches at U15 level before adding three goals in nine appearances for the U16 side.



His performances have also attracted attention at club level, where he continues to develop in Al-Nassr’s academy in Saudi Arabia. According to Portuguese outlet Zerozero, Ronaldo Jr. has scored three goals in seven appearances for the club’s youth team this season.



Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. scored a hat-trick for Al Nassr, then performed his father’s iconic “SIUUU” celebration.



The latest call-up gives him another opportunity to demonstrate his potential against international opposition. However, the attention his famous surname brings will likely attract far more scrutiny than that of many other players in the squad.



When could Cristiano Jr. make his Portugal U-17 debut?



Portugal will begin its European Championship qualifying campaign against Andorra on November 11, giving Ronaldo Jr. a potential opportunity to make his first appearance at U17 level. Filipe Ramos’ side will then face Bulgaria on November 14 before completing the group schedule against Serbia on November 17.



All three matches will take place at the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF)’s Cidade do Futebol training centre in Oeiras. Portugal must finish among the top two teams in its group to progress to the next qualifying stage, making every fixture important for Ramos’ squad.



The selection also creates a possible family reunion at the national team’s training facilities. If he receives a call-up for the Selecao’s upcoming senior international fixtures, Cristiano Ronaldo could be in the same environment as his son, although the two players will have separate schedules and commitments.



DateOpponentCompetitionNovember 11, 2026AndorraU17November 14, 2026BulgariaU17November 17, 2026SerbiaU17



Remarkable connection with Cristiano Ronaldo’s own career



There is another reason why this particular call-up has attracted attention among Portugal supporters. Ronaldo Jr. is following a remarkably similar international timeline to his father, who made his Portugal U17 debut 25 years earlier.



Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates his goal for Portugal



The senior Ronaldo subsequently progressed to the first team, making his senior Portugal debut just two years after that youth-level milestone. He went on to become the leading goalscorer in men’s international soccer, with 143 goals in 225 appearances for Portugal. The comparison is striking, although his son still has a long way to go before establishing a career of his own. 



Cristiano Ronaldo has previously made clear that he does not want his expectations to become an unnecessary burden on the teenager. “We’ll see if he’ll be a great player. He’s not yet,” Ronaldo previously said, acknowledging his son’s potential while emphasizing that talent must be supported by hard work and dedication.
